items.title: Junior Designer Wanted
items.text: Brightside Studio, a small design company in Daegu, is looking for a junior graphic designer to join its creative team. The successful candidate will create posters, social media images, and packaging for local businesses. Applicants should have a basic knowledge of design software, although previous work experience is not required. What matters more is a strong portfolio and the ability to accept feedback calmly. The position is full-time, with flexible starting hours between eight and ten in the morning. Candidates who are shortlisted will be asked to complete a short design task before the interview. Please send your portfolio and a one-page cover letter to the hiring manager by March 15. Late applications will not be considered.

items.title: An Apology for the Delay
items.text:
Dear Ms. Han,

Thank you for contacting us about your order, number 40871. I am very sorry that your desk lamp has not arrived on the promised date. Unfortunately, a storm closed the main road to our warehouse for two days, and several deliveries were affected. Your parcel left our warehouse this morning and should reach you by Friday, as we have asked the carrier to treat it as a priority. As a small apology, we have refunded the delivery fee to your card. If the lamp does not arrive by Saturday, please reply to this message and we will send a replacement at no cost.

Thank you for your patience and understanding.

Sincerely,
Joon-ho Park
Customer Care, Lumen Home

o: To ask a customer to pay a missing delivery fee
To thank a customer for choosing a new lamp
To report that the warehouse has moved elsewhere
To apologize for a late delivery and offer a fix
qs.why: 배송 지연에 대한 사과와 해결책을 알리는 이메일이에요.

The customer gave an address that was wrong
The delivery company went on a two-day strike
qs.why: a storm closed the main road라고 했어요.

items.title: Minutes of the Weekly Meeting
items.text:

1. Social media report. Daniel reported that followers grew by eight percent last month, mainly because of the short videos. The team agreed to post three videos a week instead of two.

2. Spring campaign. Priya presented two slogans. After a short discussion, the team chose the second one, which was simpler and easier to remember. Priya will ask the design team for sample posters by Friday.

items.title: Kitchen Safety Notice
items.text:
ATTENTION ALL KITCHEN STAFF

Over the past month, three small accidents have happened in our kitchen. To protect everyone, the following rules start on Monday.

First, wipe up any spilled water or oil immediately, and place a yellow warning sign on the wet floor. Second, carry knives with the blade pointing down and never leave them in a sink full of water. Third, closed, non-slip shoes must be worn at all times; sandals are not allowed, even during the break.

If you see a hazard that you cannot fix yourself, tell the head chef right away. Staff who follow the rules will help us keep a safe workplace, and the restaurant will return to its normal schedule without delays.

Thank you for your cooperation.
Chef Kwon

items.title: A Cover Letter Opening

During that time, I helped younger children choose books, repaired damaged covers, and organized a monthly reading club that now has twenty regular members.

What attracts me to this position is the chance to work with a team that values community learning. I am patient, reliable, and comfortable with basic computer systems. items.title: Working from Home Securely
items.text: Many companies now allow employees to work from home, but this freedom comes with responsibilities. When you work outside the office, you are still handling information that belongs to your employer and its customers. Experts therefore recommend a few simple habits. Use a strong password that is different for every account, and never share it, even with a colleague you trust. Avoid public Wi-Fi when you open private files, because other users on the same network may be able to see your activity. Lock your screen whenever you leave your desk, even at home, and do not discuss confidential matters where visitors can overhear you. Finally, report any suspicious email to your IT team instead of opening the attachment. A single careless click can put thousands of people's data at risk.

items.title: My Internship at a Clinic
items.text:
Last summer, I spent four weeks as an intern at a children's dental clinic. I was nervous on the first day because I had never worked in a medical setting. My supervisor, Dr. Moon, gave me a simple task: greet each family at the door and help them fill out a form. At first, my voice shook, but by the second week I was talking easily with parents and even making the children laugh.

I also learned that small details matter. A mistake in a patient's birth date, for example, can cause serious confusion later. So I started checking each form twice before handing it in. On my last day, Dr. Moon told me that this habit was the most useful thing I had shown. I did not expect such praise, and it made me think seriously about a career in healthcare.

items.title: Shadowing a Nurse for a Day
items.text:
Job shadowing means following a worker through a normal day to see what the job is really like. Hyun-woo shadowed a hospital nurse named Ms. Cho for one day, and his notes show how different the real job was from his expectations.

He had imagined that nurses spend most of their time giving injections. In fact, Ms. Cho spent much of her morning listening to patients, updating records on a tablet, and explaining medicines in simple words. She also worked closely with doctors, sharing short reports at every change of shift so that nothing important was forgotten.

At the end of the day, Hyun-woo felt tired but impressed. "I realized that communication is just as important as medical knowledge," he wrote. He has decided to take a first-aid course this winter.

items.title: Business Customs Around the World
items.text:
Doing business with people from other countries can be rewarding, but small cultural differences can cause misunderstanding. In some countries, arriving ten minutes early to a meeting shows respect. In others, the host may expect guests to arrive a little late, and starting exactly on time can feel rushed. Exchanging business cards is also treated differently. In several Asian countries, people offer and receive a card with both hands and read it carefully before putting it away. Writing on it or pushing it into a back pocket may seem impolite.

Experts advise that the best strategy is not to memorize every rule but to stay curious. Ask polite questions, watch how others behave, and be ready to adjust. Showing a sincere interest in other customs usually matters more than getting every detail right.

items.title: Feedback After Three Months
items.text:
Dear Jin-ah,

Now that you have completed your first three months with us, I would like to share some feedback. First, your work with customers has been excellent. Several of them have mentioned how patiently you explain our products, and your satisfaction scores are among the highest on the team.

There is one area where I would like to see improvement: your weekly reports. They are often submitted on Friday evening, which leaves little time for me to review them. In the coming quarter, please aim to send them by Thursday noon. If you feel overloaded, tell me early, and we can adjust your schedule together.

Overall, you have made a very good start, and I am confident that you will grow quickly. Let's meet next Monday to talk about your goals.

Best regards,
Ms. Yoon

items.title: Setting Up the Smart Speaker
items.text:
Welcome to the Aria Smart Speaker. Please follow these steps to set it up in about ten minutes.

First, place the speaker on a flat surface near a power outlet and plug it in. A blue light will appear and turn white after about thirty seconds. Next, download the Aria app on your phone and create an account. Once you have signed in, tap “Add device” and choose your speaker from the list. The app will then ask you to select your home Wi-Fi network and enter its password. After the speaker connects, it will say “Hello” to confirm that setup has been completed. Finally, open the settings menu and decide which voices the speaker may respond to. If the light turns red at any point, unplug the speaker and start again from the beginning.

items.title: Front Desk Training Guide
items.text:
Welcome to your first week at Harbor Hotel. Guests form their first impression at the front desk, so your behaviour matters a great deal.

Always greet guests with a smile within ten seconds of their arrival, even if you are on the phone. Use their family name when you have it. When a guest has a complaint, listen without interrupting, apologize for the inconvenience, and say clearly what you will do about it. Never promise something you cannot deliver; if you are unsure, say that you will check with your manager and give a time when you will reply.

Remember, too, that guest information is private. Do not say a guest's room number aloud in the lobby. Write it down and hand it over instead.

items.title: Employee of the Month
items.text:
Congratulations to Tae-min Oh, who has been named Employee of the Month for October! Tae-min works in our delivery department, where he is known for solving problems calmly. Last month, a heavy rainstorm damaged a van that was carrying forty urgent orders. Instead of waiting for repairs, Tae-min contacted nearby shops, borrowed two small vehicles, and arranged for every order to reach customers on the same day.

His manager, Ms. Baek, said, “Tae-min doesn't just follow instructions. He thinks about what the customer needs and finds a way.” Colleagues also praised him for training two new drivers without being asked.

As a reward, Tae-min will receive a gift card and an extra day of leave. The next winner will be announced on November 30, so keep up the good work, everyone!

items.title: Career Fair Announcement
items.text:
The Seoul Youth Career Fair will take place on Saturday, April 12, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. at the Riverside Convention Center. Over sixty organizations, including hospitals, technology firms, and farms, will run booths where students can ask questions about daily work and training.

New this year are fifteen-minute “job chats,” in which professionals talk about their paths to their current positions and answer questions. Spaces are limited, so students must reserve a seat on the fair's website by April 8. In addition, a free workshop will help visitors write a one-page résumé. No tickets are required, but visitors under eighteen should bring a student ID.

Please note that parking at the center is not available. Visitors are encouraged to use public transport.

items.title: Learning a Trade at School
items.text:
In recent years, more teenagers have chosen vocational high schools over traditional academic ones. Su-bin, a second-year student at a school that specializes in cooking, says she made the decision after watching her uncle run a small restaurant. "I wanted to do something practical," she explains.

Her week is divided between regular subjects and kitchen training. Twice a month, students also work at partner restaurants, where professional chefs supervise them. Su-bin admits that the early mornings are difficult, but she says the experience has changed how she sees her future. "In a normal class, you sometimes wonder why you are studying something. In the kitchen, you see the result on the plate immediately."

Educators note that such programs help students discover their strengths early, although they warn that teenagers should still keep other options open.

items.title: Reporting a Software Bug

Subject: Bug – the Save button freezes the app

While testing version 2.4 on my laptop this morning, I found a problem with the Save button. When I enter a note longer than 500 characters and press Save, the app freezes for about ten seconds and then closes without saving anything.

Steps to reproduce:

2. Paste in a text of more than 500 characters.

I tried this three times with the same result. Shorter notes work normally. Since users could lose important work, I suggest that we fix this before the release on Friday. I have attached a screen recording.

Ha-neul

items.title: Smart Farming
items.text:
Farming is changing quickly. On a strawberry farm in Nonsan, sensors placed among the plants measure temperature, moisture, and light every few minutes and send the data to a farmer's phone. If the soil becomes too dry, the system can switch on the watering equipment automatically, even in the middle of the night.

Farmer Lee Dong-gu says that the technology has not reduced his workload as much as he expected. "I still walk through the greenhouse every day," he says. "But now I know where to look." He also reports that his harvest has risen by about fifteen percent, while his water use has fallen.

Experts caution, however, that smart farms are costly to build. Young farmers often need government support to buy equipment, and learning to read the data takes time.

items.title: Conference Call Etiquette
items.text:
Conference calls save time and travel costs, but they can easily go wrong without good manners. First, join a few minutes early and test your microphone so that the meeting can start on time. Keep yourself on mute when you are not speaking, as background noise such as typing or a barking dog can distract everyone.

When you do speak, state your name briefly, particularly in a large group, because participants cannot see each other's body language. Try not to interrupt; if two people begin speaking at once, one of them should politely offer the other the chance to continue. Finally, summarize the key decisions at the end and say who will take each action. A short follow-up email that repeats these points helps to prevent confusion afterward.

items.title: Preparing for a Job Interview
items.text:
A job interview is not only a test; it is a conversation in which both sides learn about each other. The most successful candidates usually prepare in three ways.

First, they research the organization. Knowing what a company makes, whom it serves, and what it values allows you to connect your own skills with its needs. Second, they practise answering common questions aloud, such as “Tell me about a time you solved a problem.” A good answer gives a brief situation, describes the action you took, and explains the result. Third, they prepare one or two questions of their own, for example about training opportunities.

On the day, arrive ten minutes early, listen carefully, and be honest. Interviewers often remember a sincere answer longer than a perfect one.

items.title: From Truck to Customer
items.text:
Every parcel that reaches your door has passed through a chain of steps in a distribution center. When a truck arrives, workers first check the delivery note against the number of boxes to make sure nothing is missing. The goods are then unloaded and scanned, which records their arrival in the computer system.

Next, each parcel is sorted by destination. Large centers use conveyor belts and machines for this task, while smaller ones depend on workers who read the labels. Sorted parcels are placed into containers, which are loaded onto vans according to their route. Finally, drivers scan every parcel again when it leaves the building and when it reaches the customer. This final scan allows the sender to follow the delivery online.

Because mistakes at any stage can delay a parcel, workers are trained to check labels carefully and to report damaged boxes immediately.

items.title: Life as a Freelancer
items.text:
Freelancers are self-employed workers who take on jobs for different clients rather than working for one employer. Writers, designers, translators, and programmers often choose this path because it offers freedom. A freelancer can decide when and where to work, and which projects to accept.

However, this freedom comes with trade-offs. Income can change greatly from month to month, so many freelancers keep savings to cover quiet periods. They are also responsible for tasks that an employer would normally handle, such as sending invoices, paying taxes, and finding new clients. Some experienced freelancers say the hardest part is not the work itself but the discipline needed to stay organized when no one is watching.

For those who are considering this option, a sensible first step is to start part-time while keeping a regular job, and to build a reputation slowly.

items.title: A Mock Interview
items.text:
Interviewer: Thank you for coming in, Nari. Could you tell me why you applied to our travel agency?
Nari: Of course. I've always loved planning trips for my friends, and I'd like to turn that hobby into a career.
Interviewer: That's interesting. Can you give me an example of a time you solved a problem?
Nari: Last year, our school trip nearly got cancelled because the bus company made a mistake. I called two other companies and found a cheaper option within a day.
Interviewer: Impressive. How do you handle a customer who is upset?
Nari: I try to stay calm, listen until they finish, and then explain what I can do to help.
Interviewer: Good. Finally, do you have any questions for us?
Nari: Yes. What kind of training do new employees receive in their first month?
Interviewer: We offer a two-week course, followed by a mentor. I'll send details by email.

qs.q: What is the interviewer's first question about?
o: Nari's reason for applying
Nari's earlier school trips
The cost of a bus company
The training for new staff
qs.why: 첫 질문은 지원 동기예요.

qs.q: How did Nari solve the problem with the school trip?
o: She asked the school to pay more
She cancelled the trip herself
She travelled with friends by train
She found another transport company
qs.why: I called two other companies라고 했어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Nari's way of treating upset customers?
o: She avoids speaking to them directly at all
She puts listening before offering help
She gives them a refund straight away
She asks the manager to take over
qs.why: listen until they finish, and then explain에서 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: What does Nari's last question show?
o: She wants to leave the job after one month
She is interested in learning at the job
She is worried about the salary
She dislikes working with a mentor
qs.why: 교육 내용을 묻는 것은 배움에 관심이 있음을 보여 줘요.

items.title: Handing Over a Project
items.text:
Dahee: Hi Marcus, do you have a few minutes? I'm going on leave tomorrow, so I'd like to hand over the Cho account.
Marcus: Sure. Is there anything urgent?
Dahee: Just one thing. The client wants the revised brochure by Thursday, and the printer needs the final file a day before.
Marcus: So I'll have to send it on Wednesday at the latest.
Dahee: Exactly. All the files are in the shared folder called "Cho 2025", and my notes are in the first document.
Marcus: Great. Who should I contact if the client has questions about the budget?
Dahee: Talk to Ms. Park in finance. She knows the details better than I do.
Marcus: Got it. Thanks for being so organized.
Dahee: No problem. I'll check my email on Friday, just in case.

qs.q: What are the speakers mainly discussing?
o: How to design a new brochure
When to meet the client in person
Which printer is the cheapest to use
How to transfer work during a leave
qs.why: 휴가 전 업무 인수인계에 관한 대화예요.

qs.q: When must Marcus send the file to the printer?
o: On Wednesday
By Thursday night
On Tuesday
On Friday
qs.why: client deadline이 Thursday이고 인쇄소는 하루 전에 파일이 필요하니 Wednesday예요.

qs.q: Who should Marcus ask about the budget?
o: The client
Dahee
Ms. Park
The printer
qs.why: Talk to Ms. Park in finance라고 했어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Dahee?
o: She is angry about leaving her work
She will be away for several months
She has not saved any useful notes for Marcus
She is prepared and can still be reached
qs.why: 정리된 메모와 금요일 이메일 확인으로 알 수 있어요.

items.title: Asking for Time Off
items.text:
Employee: Excuse me, Ms. Lim. Do you have a moment to talk about my schedule?
Manager: Of course, Tae-yang. Please sit down.
Employee: I'd like to request three days of leave in the second week of March. My cousin is getting married overseas.
Manager: Congratulations to your family. Let me check the calendar. Hmm, we have the product launch on the twelfth.
Employee: I know. That's why I'd like to leave on the fourteenth, after the launch is over.
Manager: That should work. But would you be able to finish the monthly report before you go?
Employee: Yes, I can send it by the thirteenth.
Manager: Then I'm happy to approve it. Please fill in the leave form and submit it to HR this week.
Employee: I'll do that today. Thank you so much for understanding.

qs.q: Why does Tae-yang talk to Ms. Lim?
o: To report a mistake in the calendar
To ask for permission to take leave
To offer help with the product launch
To invite her to his cousin's wedding
qs.why: 휴가를 요청하는 대화예요.

qs.q: Why did Tae-yang choose the fourteenth?
o: The product launch will have finished
The wedding will be held on the twelfth
The monthly report is due that day
HR is closed until the fourteenth
qs.why: launch가 12일이므로 이후인 14일을 골랐어요.

qs.q: What condition does Ms. Lim set?
o: He has to find a replacement driver
He has to lead the product launch
He has to complete the monthly report
He has to work on the next weekend
qs.why: finish the monthly report before you go라고 했어요.

qs.q: What will Tae-yang do next?
o: Call his cousin overseas
Check the calendar for the launch
Fill out a leave form for HR
Send the report to the client
qs.why: fill in the leave form and submit it to HR라고 했어요.

items.q: Which closing is most suitable at the end of a formal email to a client?
o: See ya later!
Kind regards,
Bye-bye for now,
Catch you soon,
items.why: 격식 있는 이메일의 맺음말로는 Kind regards가 알맞아요. 나머지는 친구 사이의 구어체예요.

items.q: In a workplace email, “Please send the file ASAP” means that you should send it
o: after a short meeting
at the same place
with a separate note
as soon as possible
items.why: ASAP는 as soon as possible의 약어예요.

items.q: A colleague writes “FYI” before a message. What does this abbreviation stand for?
o: for your information
for your invitation
from your inbox
find your instructions
items.why: FYI는 for your information(참고로 알려 드립니다)이에요.

items.q: An invitation to a company dinner ends with “RSVP by Friday.” What are you asked to do?
o: Bring a guest to the dinner on Friday
Pay for your meal before the event
Reply to say whether you will attend
Choose a seat on the bus on Friday
items.why: RSVP는 참석 여부를 회신해 달라는 표시예요.

items.q: You “cc” your supervisor on an email. What does this mean?
o: She must reply before anyone else
She cannot see who got the email
She receives a copy of the message
She has been removed from the team
items.why: cc는 carbon copy, 참조로 사본을 보낸다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: Choose the best word: “The meeting has been ___ until next Monday because the manager is ill.”
o: postponed
interrupted
reduced
finished
items.why: postpone은 일정을 뒤로 미룬다는 뜻이에요. until next Monday와 어울려요.

items.q: Choose the best phrase: “Could you ___ a meeting with the supplier for Friday?”
o: put up
give up
take off
set up
items.why: set up a meeting은 회의를 잡다라는 뜻의 연어예요.

items.q: A person who works for a company and receives wages is called a(n)
o: employer
employee
applicant
customer
items.why: employee는 고용된 사람, employer는 고용주예요.

items.q: Which document lists a person's education and work experience for a job application?
o: A résumé
An invoice for services
The minutes of a meeting
A receipt for goods
items.why: résumé(이력서)는 학력과 경력을 정리한 문서예요.

items.q: Choose the best word: “Mr. Kim receives a fixed ___ of 3,000 dollars on the 25th of every month.”
o: receipt
invoice
salary
discount
items.why: salary는 매달 정해진 급여를 뜻해요.

items.q: The project deadline is Friday. A deadline is
o: the first day of a new project
the latest time a task must be finished
a list of people on a team
a short break between two long tasks
items.why: deadline은 마감 기한을 뜻해요.

items.q: Which sentence is the most polite way to ask a customer to wait?
o: Wait here until I call your name, and don't ask again.
You have to stand there and wait, and I am busy.
Just sit over there and stop asking me questions.
Would you mind waiting a moment, please?
items.why: Would you mind ...ing는 정중한 부탁의 표현이에요.

items.q: Choose the best phrase: “I'm writing to ___ on our phone call yesterday.”
o: give away
look up
break down
follow up
items.why: follow up on은 이전 연락의 후속 조치를 하다라는 뜻이에요.

items.q: Choose the best word: “We are running ___ of printer paper, so please order more.”
o: off
out
over
away
items.why: run out of는 ~이 떨어지다라는 뜻의 표현이에요.

items.q: Which opening is the most suitable for a formal inquiry letter?
o: Hey, what's up with all that internship stuff you do there?
So, I was kinda wondering a little bit about interns.
Yo! Tell me everything about the internship thing.
I am writing to inquire about your internship program.
items.why: 격식 있는 문의 편지는 I am writing to ...로 시작해요.

items.q: You receive an automatic “Out of Office” reply from a colleague. What does it tell you?
o: She is away and cannot answer for now
She has left the company for good
She is waiting for your reply today
She has sent your message to a client
items.why: Out of Office는 부재중이라 지금은 답하기 어렵다는 자동 응답이에요.

items.q: The manager says, “Let's get the ball rolling on the new project.” She means that they should
o: buy equipment for a game
finish the work early
begin the activity
stop the project at once
items.why: get the ball rolling은 일을 시작하다라는 관용 표현이에요.

items.q: A colleague says, “Let's touch base next week.” What does she suggest?
o: Play a game together after work
Finish all of the work before next week ends
Contact each other briefly to update
Stop working together from now on
items.why: touch base는 잠깐 연락해서 상황을 나눈다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: Choose the correct word: “She is responsible ___ the monthly report.”
o: for
of
at
with
items.why: be responsible for ~는 ~에 책임이 있다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: Choose the correct word: “He is very good ___ solving customer problems.”
o: of
with
by
at
items.why: be good at ~ing 형태로 쓰여요.

items.q: Choose the correct word: “The company is looking for a ___ person who always arrives on time.”
o: reliably
reliable
reliance
relying
items.why: 명사 person을 꾸미므로 형용사 reliable이 필요해요.

items.q: Choose the correct word: “Her ___ to the team meeting was very valuable.”
o: contribution
contribute
contributed
contributing
items.why: 소유격 her 뒤에는 명사가 와야 하므로 contribution이에요.

items.q: A sign on the floor says “CAUTION: WET FLOOR.” What should you do?
o: Clean the floor with water at once
Wait outside until the floor is dry
Walk carefully because it is slippery
Take off your shoes before you enter the room
items.why: Caution은 주의하라는 표지로, 바닥이 젖어 미끄러우니 조심해서 걸어야 해요.

items.q: A door has the sign “STAFF ONLY.” Who is allowed to enter?
o: Anyone who needs some help
Only people who work there
Customers who bring a guest
People with a ticket to enter
items.why: Staff only는 직원만 출입할 수 있다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: Which email subject line is the clearest for asking to move a meeting?
o: Something I wanted to ask you about soon
Urgent!!! Please read this message right now
Meeting stuff and other related things for later
Request to reschedule Tuesday's 3 p.m. meeting
items.why: 구체적인 목적과 시간을 알려 주는 제목이 가장 분명해요.

items.q: Which action is the safest way to handle your work account password?
o: Write it on a note stuck to your monitor
Share it with a busy colleague to save time
Choose your birthday so it is easy to recall
Use a different password for each account
items.why: 계정마다 다른 비밀번호를 쓰는 것이 안전해요.

items.q: Your manager asks, “Could you send me the report by noon?” Which reply is the most appropriate?
o: Why don't you ask someone else to do it?
Certainly. I'll send it before twelve.
No, I really hate writing reports at all.
Not my job, so I'm not going to do it.
items.why: 정중하고 분명하게 수락하는 응답이 적절해요.

items.q: Which job fits this duty: “answers customers' questions by phone and solves their problems”?
o: Accountant for a bank
Architect for houses
Librarian at a school
Customer service agent
items.why: 고객 문의에 응대하는 직무는 고객 서비스 담당자예요.

items.q: Which phrase best completes the email? “Thank you for your quick reply. I ___ your help.”
o: really appreciate
am really appreciating
really appreciates
really to appreciate
items.why: appreciate는 감사 표현으로 쓰이고 주어 I 뒤에 원형이 와요.

items.good: Had I known about the deadline, I would have started earlier.
items.ko: 마감일을 알았더라면 더 일찍 시작했을 텐데요.
bad: If I knew about the deadline, I would have started earlier.
Had I knew about the deadline, I would have started earlier.
Had I known about the deadline, I would started earlier.

cz.st: ___ I known about the deadline, I would have started earlier.

items.rule: 과거 사실의 반대를 나타내는 가정법 과거완료에서 if를 생략하면 Had + 주어 + p.p. 순서로 도치돼요.

items.good: The manager asked whether I could attend the meeting.
items.ko: 관리자는 내가 회의에 참석할 수 있는지 물었어요.
bad: The manager asked whether could I attend the meeting.
The manager asked whether I could attending the meeting.
The manager asked whether I attend could the meeting.

cz.st: The manager asked whether I ___ attend the meeting.

items.rule: 간접의문문에서는 whether 뒤에 평서문 어순(주어 + 동사)을 써요.

items.good: The report must be submitted by Friday.
bad: The report must submit by Friday.
The report must be submit by Friday.
The report must been submitted by Friday.

cz.st: The report must be ___ by Friday.

items.rule: 조동사의 수동태는 조동사 + be + 과거분사로 써요.

items.good: She suggested that we hold the meeting online.
items.ko: 그녀는 우리가 회의를 온라인으로 열자고 제안했어요.
bad: She suggested us to hold the meeting online.
She suggested to hold the meeting online.
She suggested that we to hold the meeting online.

cz.st: She suggested that we ___ the meeting online.

items.rule: suggest 뒤에는 that절(주어 + 동사원형)이나 동명사를 쓰고 to부정사는 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: The candidate whose résumé impressed us most has accepted the offer.
items.ko: 이력서가 우리에게 가장 깊은 인상을 준 지원자가 제안을 수락했어요.
bad: The candidate who résumé impressed us most has accepted the offer.
The candidate whose his résumé impressed us most has accepted the offer.
The candidate whom résumé impressed us most has accepted the offer.

cz.st: The candidate ___ résumé impressed us most has accepted the offer.

items.rule: 소유를 나타내는 관계대명사는 whose이며, 뒤에 소유격 대명사를 또 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: She is interested in working for an international company.
items.ko: 그녀는 국제적인 회사에서 일하는 데 관심이 있어요.
bad: She is interested in work for an international company.
She is interested in to work for an international company.
She is interested in works for an international company.

cz.st: She is interested in ___ for an international company.

items.hint: 전치사 다음에 오는 동사의 형태를 생각해 보세요.

items.good: I wish I had more time to prepare for the presentation.
items.ko: 발표를 준비할 시간이 더 있으면 좋겠어요.
bad: I wish I have more time to prepare for the presentation.
I wish I having more time to prepare for the presentation.
I wish I will have more time to prepare for the presentation.

cz.st: I wish I ___ more time to prepare for the presentation.

items.rule: 현재 사실과 반대되는 소망은 wish + 과거형으로 나타내요.

items.good: Having finished the report, she sent it to her supervisor.
items.ko: 보고서를 끝낸 뒤에 그녀는 그것을 상사에게 보냈어요.
bad: Having finish the report, she sent it to her supervisor.
Finished the report, she sent it to her supervisor.
Having finishing the report, she sent it to her supervisor.

cz.st: ___ the report, she sent it to her supervisor.

items.rule: 먼저 일어난 일은 완료 분사구문 Having + p.p.로 나타내요.
